tool_input.command:
mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/internal-http.md <<'EOF'
# Plain HTTP for internal hosts

The project's current recorded decision is that HTTPS is used everywhere, with no plain-text exception, and that includes internal hosts. Certificate management is already in place, so internal hosts are served over HTTPS like any other.
EOF
cat docs/policies/internal-http.md

result:
I created `docs/policies/internal-http.md`. It says the current decision is HTTPS everywhere with no plain-text exception, internal hosts included, because certificate management is already in place. It doesn't mention the earlier plain-HTTP position.

Muninn holds two conflicting records on this. An earlier one (#13) allowed plain HTTP for internal hosts because they sit behind the firewall. A later one (#32, recorded about six minutes after) says HTTPS everywhere and explicitly replaces the plain-HTTP position. I went with #32 as current because it is the newer record and names the one it replaces.

Muninn still flags both as active, and both are only trust 1, seen in transcripts rather than user-confirmed. If #13 should stand instead, the file needs changing.
